title: docs(qa): api-backend checklist says what each pin asserts and at which layer (18.2.0 sweep, 28 lines)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9VvigEWYo4KrkZvUgfw5EG6)_
Fixes #25837

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Wave anchor: #25807 (the 18.2.0 release test sweep; it stays open).

## What changes

One file, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json`. Fourteen items are revised from the 28 checklist-accuracy lines of QA runs #25815 (`release-18.2.0-tier1`) and #25817 (`release-18.2.0-manual-set`), both at `6679644a`. Each revised item bumps `revision` by one and appends one `history` row that cites its run record and the findings it applies. No clause, oracle or priority changed. Every line was re-read against `origin/main` at `f6c61932` before it was edited.

Most lines are one shape: an item's `automated.ref` or a clause's `verify` said a pin covered more than the pin asserts, or did not say which layer the pin reaches. Under RUNNER rule 6 a pin scores only the layer it drives, so the edits name that layer (unit, engine, or HTTP) and say which half of each clause the live run still owes.

| Item | Findings | Edit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `action-activation-door-contract` | a2, a5, a6 | knownGaps[0], acceptance[2], [5] and [6] verify, `automated.ref`: the 400s are asserted by code only (no `fields[0]`, no non-object-body case); the ledger pin finds the row with `rows.find` and checks the flip's status, not its body; the ambiguity case asserts only the twin's name `crm_account`. Names `field-error-code-catalog.test.ts` as a unit read of the shared body reader. |
| `bulk-write-contract` | ref, a3 | `automated.ref`: the dogfood file's bulk cases are engine calls (`ql.update` / `ql.delete` with `multi: true`), not the HTTP bulk doors, so it scores no clause; adds `rest-batch-size-cap.test.ts` as unit evidence for a3, partial at most. |
| `data-request-shape-and-query-arity` | a1–a4, a1 | `automated.ref` names the layer of every file (none boots the Hono adapter, so they score a0 only) and adds `data-update-expected-version.test.ts`; acceptance[1].verify says the empty-token leg is the PATCH door's. |
| `declarative-endpoint-execution` | a1, a2 | acceptance[1] and [2] verify, `automated.ref`: no pin asserts the 401's code; gate (a) asserts the fix sentence (script) and the SSRF reason (proxy), never the endpoint's name; the #5488 withdrawal and the CLI refusal are the run's. |
| `error-sentences-and-unique-violation-wire-code` | a1, a2 | acceptance[1] and [2] verify: the hook-envelope pin calls `mapDataError` directly (unit); the unique-violation pin is `HttpDispatcher` over a real engine and SqlDriver, no Hono. |
| `meta-read-doors-v18` | a4, a1–a3 | acceptance[4].verify and `automated.ref`: adds `showcase-fls-read-mask-strip.dogfood.test.ts` for the data-sort 403; every other pin drives the protocol, route handlers or the dispatcher with a stub server, so a1–a3 are live legs. |
| `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch` | a0, a3/a6/n1 | acceptance[0].verify and `automated.ref`: the dogfood asserts 409 and `/ACTION_DISABLED\|is disabled/` only; the exact sentence and the 403, flow-type and absence legs are pinned by a unit `HttpDispatcher` over fakes. |
| `query-contract-matrix` | a4, n0, whole item | `automated.ref`: the `[#2850]` case proves middleware routing on a mock driver, not a withheld contact over HTTP; the request-schema pin is a mocked protocol; no clause has a pin at its oracle's layer, so every clause runs live. `automated` is kept: the pins are real evidence of their layers. |
| `rest-batch-config-contract` | a5 | acceptance[5].verify: §E asserts the key plus `/never built/` and `/options.atomic/`, never `BatchEndpointsConfigSchema` or the upsert replacement. |
| `rest-crud-config-contract` | a3, a4 | `automated.ref` and acceptance[4].verify: adds `discovery-services-route-follows-mount.test.ts` for the advertisement half of a3 (the moved route table has no pin); §E never matches the declarative-endpoint prescription. |
| `rest-metadata-config-contract` | a1, a3, a5 | `automated.ref` and acceptance[5].verify: §D pins prefix survival through `normalizeConfig`, not a mount; adds the discovery pin for a1's advertisement half and `meta-object-fls.test.ts` for a3's masking effect at the route-handler layer; §E never asserts the replacement. |
| `rest-route-generation-tombstones` | a0 | `automated.ref`: §E matches `/was removed/`, not the clause's `was removed in @objectstack/spec 17`. |
| `aggregate-contract-matrix` | #25817 | negative[2]: the #24618 negative-offset shift no longer reproduces (re-measured by #25817 under UTC, America/Los_Angeles and Pacific/Auckland); #24618 is closed as completed. |
| `formula-stdlib-matrix` | #25817 | fixtures.requires[1], steps[5] and steps[6]: every scratch object declares a `sharingModel`, or an active save answers 422 `security-owd-unset` before the formula is judged. |

### Lines not applied as written

- `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch` a5: the record says the ref is correct that the restart leg stays manual. Nothing to change; the sentence is unchanged.
- `data-request-shape-and-query-arity` a1 asked whether the clause meant DELETE for the empty token. It means PATCH (steps[1]). The PATCH refusal is pinned in `data-update-expected-version.test.ts`, which the ref did not name; the edit adds it rather than re-pointing the clause.
- `rest-metadata-config-contract` a1 and a3 are applied, but the tree is narrower than the record on two points. `discovery-services-route-follows-mount.test.ts` does read `routes.metadata` at prefix `/metadata` (it was outside the ref). `meta-object-fls.test.ts` does pin the masking effect and the `maskObjectFields: false` opt-out, at the route-handler layer. Both are now named, with the layer they score.
- `formula-stdlib-matrix`: the record names steps[5] and requires[1]. steps[6] is edited too: its active-door probe also reads a 422, and without a `sharingModel` it would capture `security-owd-unset` instead of the expression refusal.

No line turned out to be a product defect, so no card is owed from this PR. The retired `objectui:build` / `.objectui-sha` / pin-script wording does not occur in this file (0 hits), so nothing was carried over from #26035.

Docs-only: the ledger is not in any package's `files[]`, so this PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

- Three lines of `api-console-discovery-execute` still spell the Console sources as the sibling repo, `objectui apps/console/src/pages/developer/…`. Those files now live under `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/`. This is path spelling, not the retired pin wording, and it is outside this card's lines. Carrier: none.
